examples.ko: 이사 가기 전에 도배를 새로 했어요.
examples.en: I had the walls newly papered before moving.
After wallpapering, there is a smell of paste.

examples.ko: 벽지 값보다 도배 비용이 더 비싸요.
examples.en: The wallpapering cost is higher than the price of the wallpaper.
After the wallpapering was done, the room brightened up.

examples.ko: 도배 기술자가 하루 만에 방을 끝냈어요.
examples.en: The wallpapering worker finished the room in one day.
Mold has formed, so the walls need new wallpaper.

explain: '도배'는 '벽지', '장판'과 함께 집 공사 이야기에서 자주 나와요. 인터넷에서 같은 글을 계속 올리는 것도 '도배'라고 해서, 앞뒤 말을 보고 구분해요.
explain_en: '도배' often appears alongside '벽지' and '장판' when talking about home renovation. Posting the same message over and over online is also called '도배', so tell them apart from the context.

examples.en: We rented the whole pension and had fun as a family.

examples.ko: 독채라서 소음 걱정 없이 지낼 수 있어요.
examples.en: It's a standalone house, so you can stay without worrying about noise.
This house is a whole-house jeonse, so it's expensive.
I booked a whole hanok house for our stay.

examples.ko: 독채를 쓰니까 마당도 마음대로 쓸 수 있어요.
examples.en: Since we use the whole house, we can use the yard freely too.

examples.ko: 원룸 말고 독채로 이사 가고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to move into a standalone house instead of a studio.

explain: 다른 사람과 나누지 않고 건물 한 채를 통째로 쓰는 것을 말해요. 방 하나만 빌리는 경우와 비교할 때 써요. 펜션이나 한옥 숙소를 예약할 때 자주 보이는 말이에요.
explain_en: It means using a whole building by yourself without sharing it with others. It's used in contrast with renting just one room. You often see it when booking a pension or hanok stay.

examples.en: I watered the plants with a watering can.
I left the watering can on the balcony.
The watering can is old and its holes are clogged.

examples.ko: 물뿌리개 대신 페트병으로 물을 줘도 돼요.
examples.en: You can water plants with a plastic bottle instead of a watering can.
Water comes out gently from this watering can.
Please fill the watering can with water.

explain: 꽃이나 화분에 물을 줄 때 쓰는 도구예요. 일상에서는 '물조리개'라고도 말해요. 주로 '물뿌리개로 물을 주다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is the tool used to water flowers and pots. In daily talk it is also called '물조리개'. It is mostly used as '물뿌리개로 물을 주다'.

examples.en: I put a banana and milk in the blender and blended them.
The blender was so loud that the baby woke up.
I blend fruit in the blender to make juice.

examples.ko: 새 믹서를 사고 싶은데 추천해 주세요.
examples.en: I want to buy a new blender, so please recommend one.
Close the blender lid and press the button.
The blender gets louder when you add ice.

explain: 집에서 과일이나 채소를 가는 기계는 '블렌더'보다 '믹서'라고 부르는 일이 더 익숙해요. 보통 '믹서에 갈다', '믹서로 갈다'처럼 '갈다'와 같이 쓰고, 반죽을 섞는 기계와는 달라요.
explain_en: For the kitchen machine that grinds fruit or vegetables, Koreans are used to calling it a '믹서' rather than a 'blender'. It usually goes with '갈다' (to grind), as in '믹서에 갈다'.

examples.en: The floor is cold, so please put down a cushion and sit.
I gave the guest a cushion.
This cushion is thick and soft.
A cushion is placed on the chair.
At the restaurant, we sit on cushions to eat.
Grandma's cushion has a pretty flower pattern.

explain: 방석은 바닥에 앉을 때 깔고, 의자에 놓는 것은 '쿠션'이라고 부르는 경우가 많아요. 한국 식당이나 집에서 바닥에 앉을 때 손님에게 방석을 내줘요. '방석을 깔다', '방석에 앉다'로 써요.
explain_en: 방석 is what you put down to sit on the floor; a soft pad for a chair is often called a 쿠션. In Korean homes and restaurants with floor seating, hosts hand guests a 방석. Typical verbs are 방석을 깔다 and 방석에 앉다.

examples.en: This defeat was a painful experience for us.
That mistake still stings me even now.

examples.ko: 그 말을 들으니 뼈아프지만 맞는 말이에요.
examples.en: Hearing it hurts deeply, but it's true.
I regretted it bitterly, but it was already too late.
The chance we missed in the final really hurt.

examples.ko: 이번 일이 뼈아프다고 해서 포기할 필요는 없어요.
examples.en: Just because this hurts doesn't mean you need to give up.

explain: 몸이 아픈 게 아니라 실수, 패배, 손실, 후회가 뼈에 사무칠 만큼 마음에 크게 와닿을 때 써요. '뼈아픈 실수, 뼈아픈 패배, 뼈아픈 교훈'처럼 쓰고, '뼈저리다'와 비슷해요.
explain_en: It does not mean physical pain but a mistake, defeat, loss or regret that cuts to the bone emotionally. It appears in phrases like '뼈아픈 실수', '뼈아픈 패배' and '뼈아픈 교훈', and is similar to '뼈저리다'.

examples.en: At the countryside house, we turn on the oil heater in winter.
We roasted and ate sweet potatoes next to the oil heater.

examples.ko: 석유난로를 켜 놓고 잘 때는 환기해야 해요.
examples.en: When you leave an oil heater on and sleep, you need to ventilate.
Please put oil into the oil heater.
There is an oil heater in the room at Grandma's house.
An electric heater is more convenient than an oil heater.

explain: 석유난로에 넣는 기름은 보통 '등유'라고 해요. 불을 쓰는 난로라서 환기와 안전에 꼭 주의해야 해요.
explain_en: The fuel put into an oil heater is usually called '등유' (kerosene). Because it uses a flame, you must be careful about ventilation and safety.

examples.en: Thanks to the dishwasher, the time I spend on dishes has gone down.
I put the dishes in the dishwasher and pressed the button.
The new house comes with a dishwasher.

examples.ko: 이 냄비는 식기세척기로 씻으면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't wash this pot in the dishwasher.
The dishwasher is too noisy.
I compared prices because I want to buy a dishwasher.

explain: 말할 때는 줄여서 '식세기'라고 하는 사람이 많아요. '설거지'와 함께 외워 두면 좋고, '식기세척기를 돌리다'라고 자주 말해요.
explain_en: In speech many people shorten it to '식세기'. It pairs well with '설거지' (washing dishes), and people often say '식기세척기를 돌리다' for running it.

examples.en: When the accident happened, the airbag deployed.

examples.ko: 새 차에는 에어백이 여섯 개 있어요.
examples.en: The new car has six airbags.
Thanks to the airbag, I was not badly hurt.
I went to have the driver's airbag inspected.

examples.ko: 에어백이 있어도 안전벨트는 꼭 매야 해요.
examples.en: Even with an airbag, you must wear a seat belt.

examples.ko: 차를 살 때 에어백 개수를 비교했어요.
examples.en: When buying a car, I compared the number of airbags.

explain: 자동차 사고 때 몸을 보호하는 공기주머니예요. 에어백은 안전벨트와 함께 써야 효과가 있어서, 둘을 한 쌍으로 말하는 경우가 많아요. '터지다'나 '작동하다'와 같이 써요.
explain_en: An air cushion in a car that protects the body in a crash. It works properly only together with a seat belt, so the two are often mentioned as a pair. It pairs with verbs like 터지다 and 작동하다.

examples.ko: 빵을 굽기 전에 오븐을 먼저 예열해요.
examples.en: I preheat the oven before baking bread.

examples.ko: 팬을 충분히 예열한 다음에 기름을 두르세요.
examples.en: Heat the pan well first, and then add the oil.

examples.ko: 오븐을 예열하는 동안 반죽을 만들어 볼까요?
examples.en: Shall we make the dough while the oven preheats?
I forgot to preheat, so the cake came out undercooked.

examples.ko: 히터가 엔진을 예열해 줘서 시동이 잘 걸려요.
examples.en: The heater warms up the engine, so the car starts well.
Ten minutes of preheating is enough, so don't worry.

explain: 요리나 기계를 쓰기 전에 미리 데운다는 뜻으로 써요. 레시피에서 '예열해 두세요'처럼 자주 나와요. '데우다'는 식은 음식에도 쓰지만 '예열하다'는 오븐, 팬, 엔진처럼 쓰기 전 준비 단계에만 써요.
explain_en: It means to heat something ahead of use in cooking or machines. Recipes often say '예열해 두세요'. '데우다' also applies to reheating cold food, but '예열하다' is only for the preparation step before using an oven, pan or engine.

examples.en: I lay down in the ondol room of the hanok and my back felt warm.

examples.ko: 이 펜션은 온돌방과 침대방이 따로 있어요.
examples.en: This pension has separate ondol rooms and bed rooms.
In winter an ondol room is the best.
The floor of the ondol room at Grandma's house is toasty hot.
If you book an ondol room, you sleep on bedding laid on the floor.

examples.ko: 외국인 친구들이 온돌방 체험을 해 보고 싶대요.
examples.en: My foreign friends say they want to try an ondol room.

explain: 바닥 아래로 따뜻한 열이 지나가게 만든 한국식 방이에요. 숙소에서는 침대 없이 바닥에 이불을 깔고 자는 방을 '온돌방'이라고 해요. 침대가 있는 방은 '침대방'이라고 구분해요.
explain_en: It is a Korean-style room where warmth passes under the floor. At lodgings, an '온돌방' is a room where you sleep on bedding laid on the floor with no bed. Rooms with beds are distinguished as '침대방'.

examples.en: With the fan heater on in the office, it's warm.
My throat is dry because of the fan heater's air.

examples.ko: 교실 온풍기가 고장 나서 모두 외투를 입고 있어요.
examples.en: The classroom heater broke, so everyone is wearing coats.
I sat next to the heater and now I'm sleepy.

examples.ko: 작은 온풍기를 하나 사서 발밑에 두었어요.
examples.en: I bought a small fan heater and put it under my feet.
Fan heaters use a lot of electricity, so be careful.

explain: 더운 바람을 내보내서 공간을 데우는 난방 기구예요. 겨울철 사무실이나 교실에서 흔하고, 바닥을 데우는 '온돌'이나 '보일러'와는 방식이 달라요. 에어컨의 난방 기능을 말할 때는 '온풍'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is a heater that warms a space by blowing hot air. It is common in offices and classrooms in winter and works differently from floor heating ('온돌') or a '보일러'. The heating mode of an air conditioner is also called '온풍'.

en: be tidied up; be in order

examples.ko: 방이 깨끗하게 정돈돼 있어서 기분이 좋아요.
examples.en: The room is neatly in order, so I feel good.
When the desk is tidy, studying goes better.
My thoughts were not in order, so I talked for too long.

examples.ko: 잘 정돈된 옷장은 옷을 찾기 쉬워요.
examples.en: A well-organized closet makes it easy to find clothes.
Please wait until the documents are in order.

examples.ko: 마음이 정돈되고 나니 결정을 내릴 수 있었어요.
examples.en: After my mind settled, I was able to make a decision.

explain: 정돈되다는 흩어진 것이 제자리에 놓여 깔끔하다는 말이에요. 방이나 서류뿐 아니라 '생각이 정돈되다'처럼 마음에도 써요. 일상에서는 '정리되다'를 더 자주 써요.
explain_en: 정돈되다 means scattered things are put in place and neat. It applies to rooms and papers, and also to the mind, as in '생각이 정돈되다'. In daily talk 정리되다 is more common.

examples.en: It's an old house, so we need to do repairs.
This weekend I did home repairs with my father.
The home repair cost more than I thought.
It was noisy all day because of the home repair work.

examples.ko: 집수리를 맡길 만한 업체를 찾고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm looking for a company I can trust with home repairs.

examples.ko: 비가 새서 급하게 집수리 기사님을 불렀어요.
examples.en: The roof leaked, so I urgently called a home repair technician.

explain: 고장 난 곳을 고치는 작은 일부터 집 안을 새로 꾸미는 큰 공사까지 넓게 말할 때 써요. '집수리를 하다/맡기다'로 쓰고, 큰 공사는 '리모델링'이라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It covers everything from small fixes of broken spots to larger work on a home. Use it as '집수리를 하다/맡기다'. For big jobs people also say '리모델링' (remodeling).

examples.en: After showering, I dried my body with a towel.
The hotel brought me a fresh towel.
When I work out, I wrap a towel around my neck.
Can I borrow a towel at the pool?

examples.ko: 이 타월은 부드럽고 물을 잘 빨아들여요.
examples.en: This towel is soft and absorbs water well.
I hung the wet towel out in the sun.

explain: 집에서는 보통 '수건'이라고 하고, '타월'은 호텔, 수영장, 운동 용품에서 자주 써요. 둘 다 같은 물건이지만 '타월'은 외래어라 조금 더 상품 이름 느낌이에요. 목욕탕의 '때수건'은 '이태리타월'이라고도 불러요.
explain_en: At home people usually say 수건, while 타월 is more common for hotels, pools and sports goods. They refer to the same item, but 타월 is a loanword and feels a bit more like a product name. The scrubbing cloth in a bathhouse is called 이태리타월.

examples.en: You need a saw to cut a tree.
My father is cutting a board with a saw.

examples.ko: 이 톱은 날이 무뎌서 잘 안 잘려요.
examples.en: This saw has a dull blade, so it doesn't cut well.

examples.ko: 톱질을 하다 손을 다치지 않게 조심하세요.
examples.en: Be careful not to hurt your hand while sawing.
I found an old saw in the storage room.

examples.ko: 톱의 날에 녹이 슬어서 새로 바꿨어요.
examples.en: The saw blade had rusted, so I replaced it.

explain: '톱질하다'가 톱으로 자르는 동작이에요. 톱으로 나무를 길게 가르는 건 '켜다'라고도 해요. 영어 top에서 온 '톱 뉴스', '톱 클래스'의 '톱'과 소리가 같지만 다른 단어예요.
explain_en: The action of cutting with a saw is 톱질하다, and splitting wood lengthwise with one is also called 켜다. It sounds the same as the 톱 from English top in '톱 뉴스' and '톱 클래스', but it is a different word.

examples.en: The baby fell asleep snugly in her mother's arms.
I took a nap warmly tucked under the blanket.
When snow fell, the village was softly covered.
Grandmother held me in a warm, soft hug.
The sunlight shone gently into the room.
Wrapped cozily in a blanket, the cold went away.

explain: 몸이 따뜻하고 부드럽게 감싸이는 편안한 느낌을 말해요. 이불, 품, 햇살, 분위기처럼 부드럽고 따뜻한 것과 잘 어울려요. 형용사 '포근하다'에서 온 말이라 날씨가 춥지 않고 부드러울 때도 '포근하다'를 써요.
explain_en: It conveys the comfortable feeling of being wrapped warmly and softly. It goes well with things like blankets, embraces, sunlight and atmosphere. It comes from the adjective '포근하다', which is also used for mild, soft weather.

examples.ko: 이 침대는 폭신해서 자도 허리가 안 아파요.
examples.en: This bed is soft, so my back doesn't hurt after sleeping.
My feet feel comfortable in these soft slippers.
The cake sponge is very soft.
I wonder how to cook a fluffy rolled omelet.

examples.ko: 소파가 너무 폭신하면 오래 앉기 힘들어요.
examples.en: If a sofa is too soft, it's hard to sit for long.
The path covered in fallen leaves feels soft.

explain: '푹신하다'와 거의 같게 쓰는데, '폭신하다'가 좀 더 가볍고 작은 느낌이에요. 사람의 성격이 아니라 침대, 빵, 눈길처럼 닿는 느낌에 써요.
explain_en: It is used almost the same as '푹신하다', but '폭신하다' feels a bit lighter and smaller. It describes how something feels to the touch, like beds, bread or snowy paths, not a person's personality.

examples.en: The new computer has a very fast processor.
The processor is hot, so the fan keeps spinning.
I compared the processors of phones.
The better the processor performance, the smoother the game.

examples.ko: 이 노트북은 프로세서를 바꿀 수 없어요.
examples.en: You can't swap the processor in this laptop.
The company announced a new processor this year.

explain: 프로세서는 컴퓨터나 휴대폰 안에서 계산과 명령을 처리하는 부품이에요. 보통 'CPU'라고도 하는데, 프로세서는 더 넓게 쓰여서 그래픽 처리 같은 다른 처리 장치도 포함할 수 있어요. 일상에서는 '칩'이라고 줄여서 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: A 프로세서 is the part inside a computer or phone that handles calculations and commands. It is often called a 'CPU', but 프로세서 is the broader term and can include other processing units such as graphics. In casual talk people sometimes just say '칩'.
